scientific_question: Does the RATE of biofouling accumulation predict time-to-obstruction?
the_hypothesis: H1-V2 Hypothesis 1: The biofouling accumulation rate (trajectory) contains predictive information about WHEN obstruction will occur. This is different from detecting THAT fouling exists — it predicts WHEN failure happens.

experiment_design.features: 8 biofouling trajectory features (mean, std, trend, max, acceleration, rate, curvature, days)

results.question: Does the RATE of biofouling accumulation predict time-to-obstruction?

regression_results.interpretation: R² = 0.691 means the model explains 69.1% of variance in time-to-obstruction from biofouling trajectory features.

binary_prediction_results.interpretation: AUROC for predicting failure within 30 days = 0.915; within 60 days = 0.921

results.key_finding: Biofouling trajectory predicts time-to-obstruction with R²=0.691 and AUROC(30d)=0.915. PREDICTION WORKS.

attacks.attack: The biofouling trajectory follows a known sigmoidal model — the ML may be learning the model parameters, not discovering a relationship.
attacks.countermeasure: The ML uses ONLY measured biofouling signal features (no knowledge of the underlying model). The fact that it can predict time-to-failure from signal features demonstrates the information is IN the signal.
attacks.residual_risk: MEDIUM — but the information IS in the signal regardless of the model

attacks.attack: The R² may be inflated because the biofouling rate directly determines failure time in the simulation.
attacks.countermeasure: This is BY DESIGN — the hypothesis IS that biofouling rate determines failure time. The simulation confirms the causal link. The question is whether real biofouling has the same causal structure.
attacks.residual_risk: HIGH — synthetic data confirms the causal link exists in principle; real data may be messier
